points.summary: DeSaulnier advocates for workers to have a voice as AI and automation reshape the economy. He supports protecting the right to organize, safe workplaces, living wages, and has authored legislation to tax excessive CEO pay and protect workers from mass layoffs.
points.quote: Pushing to ensure workers have a real voice as AI reshapes their industries.

points.summary: DeSaulnier prioritizes expanding affordable housing and reducing housing costs through transit-oriented development, federal investments, and research on telework to reduce congestion. He previously created a permanent funding source for affordable housing as a State Senator.
points.quote: Advancing transit-oriented housing through the Equitable Transit Oriented Development Support Act and fighting for federal investments that bring down housing costs.

points.summary: DeSaulnier fights to protect California's vehicle emission standards and clean energy investments against federal rollbacks. He advocates for Delta water protection, fossil fuel worker transition programs, and opposes attempts to undermine federal land protections.
points.quote: Fighting to protect California’s vehicle emission standards and clean energy investments against federal rollbacks.

points.summary: DeSaulnier positions himself as the top Democrat on the House Ethics Committee, holding Congress to higher standards. He emphasizes transparency through over 260 town halls and ensuring constituents have direct access to their representative and answers.
points.quote: Holding Congress to a higher standard and making sure the people I represent always have access to me—and answers when they need them.

points.summary: DeSaulnier fights to protect NIH and medical research funding, having been personally saved by federally funded cancer research. He advocates for expanding access to quality care and improving patient navigation through the healthcare system after a diagnosis.
points.quote: Fighting against any cuts to medical research funding that would slow the development of new treatments and cures.

points.summary: DeSaulnier supports evidence-based gun violence reduction, including funding research on what works, investing in gun safety technology, and enabling communities to share effective local strategies. He supported the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
points.quote: Pushing to fund research on what works to reduce gun violence, invest in technology that prevents unauthorized use, and make it easier for communities to share effective local strategies.

points.summary: DeSaulnier fights to codify reproductive rights into federal law, opposing any federal legislation that would restrict women's access to healthcare or override California's protections. He also sponsors legislation on contraception and IVF access.
points.quote: Fighting to codify reproductive rights into federal law.

points.summary: DeSaulnier pushes for humane, fair, and functional immigration reform. He opposes mass deportation policies, demands accountability for ICE actions, and advocates for dignity for families already living and contributing in the community.
points.quote: Pushing for humane, fair, and functional immigration reform that reflects American values.

pages.title: Frese For Congress

points.summary: Congress should not be a career. The campaign supports 8-year term limits, banning members of Congress from trading stocks, a no-budget-no-pay rule, and closing the revolving door so former members cannot cash out as lobbyists.
points.quote: 8-year term limits. Congress was never meant to be a career.

points.summary: California housing is unaffordable due to deficit spending, slow building, and institutional investors. The campaign pledges to stop deficit spending that drives mortgage rates, cut red tape on building, ban Wall Street and hedge funds from buying single-family homes, and block foreign ownership of farmland and family homes.
points.quote: Ban Wall Street and hedge funds from buying single-family homes.

points.summary: Every neighborhood should feel safe after dark. The campaign backs police, ending cashless bail, keeping repeat offenders off the streets, enforcing real consequences for fentanyl dealers, and keeping boys out of girls' sports.
points.quote: End cashless bail. Consequences can't be optional.

points.summary: Election integrity is foundational. The campaign supports making Election Day a national holiday, requiring voter ID for federal elections, same-day voting with ID, keeping vote by mail, using paper ballots as a permanent audit trail, and ensuring transparent auditable results.
points.quote: Make Election Day a national holiday.

points.summary: Schools should prepare kids for real life. The campaign supports eliminating federal income tax on teachers, directing money to classrooms rather than bureaucrats, focusing on reading, math, history, and civics, bringing back shop class and trades, preparing students for automation and AI, and keeping parents in charge.
points.quote: No federal income tax on teachers.

points.summary: Social Security and Medicare are earned benefits that Washington should not touch. The campaign pledges no cuts, no raising the retirement age, investing part of the trust fund in the S&P 500, and going after fraud and waste to protect benefits for Americans who paid in.
points.quote: No cuts. You earned it.

points.summary: Parents have a right to see what their children are taught in school. The campaign frames parental oversight of curriculum as a baseline right and positions itself against an opponent who voted against such transparency measures.
points.quote: Parents have a right to see what their kids are taught.

points.summary: Lateefah will champion legislation closing loopholes in federal gun laws, stopping illegal firearms flow into communities, and providing resources for mental health, addiction treatment, and recidivism prevention programs. She also advocates progressive policing models like non-sworn transit ambassadors and crisis intervention specialists.
points.quote: Lateefah will champion legislation that closes loopholes in federal gun laws, stops the flow of illegal firearms into the community

points.summary: Housing is framed as a fundamental right. Lateefah will pursue $4.5 billion for permanent supportive housing, expand the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, increase rental subsidies, end landlord discrimination, and support building 3 million homes over four years with first-time buyer assistance.
points.quote: Housing is a fundamental right, and real solutions are needed to address the housing crisis in our district.

points.summary: Lateefah will leverage federal funds to convert empty government buildings into dignified emergency shelters, build more transitional housing units in the East Bay, and increase federal aid for mental health and social worker staffing at the frontlines of the homelessness crisis.
points.quote: she will fight to leverage federal funds to transform empty government buildings like the old County Jail in Oakland into dignified emergency shelters

points.summary: Lateefah supports a living wage, aid to small businesses, infrastructure investment for job creation, banning corporate price-gouging to lower grocery prices, and ensuring the wealthiest Americans and corporations pay their fair share to reduce income inequality.
points.quote: She supports a living wage, aid to small businesses, and investment in infrastructure projects that create jobs and stimulate local economies.

points.summary: Lateefah advocates for a public option and ultimately an affordable single-payer health system. She will expand Medicare drug price negotiation to all drugs, close the Medicaid coverage gap, expand Medicare to dental/vision/hearing, lower the Medicare eligibility age, and invest in maternal and infant mortality reduction.
points.quote: advocating for a public option and ultimately working towards an affordable single-payer health system

points.summary: Lateefah will fight to restore and protect a woman's right to choose, guaranteeing safe and legal abortion access for every woman regardless of location or income. She will push back against every effort to strip away reproductive rights.
points.quote: she will fight like hell alongside Democrats to win back a woman’s right to choose

points.summary: Lateefah will support legislation to prohibit the federal death penalty and require re-sentencing of those currently on death row. She draws on her experience creating the Back on Track anti-recidivism program and her work empowering survivors of trafficking and violence.
points.quote: She will support legislation to prohibit the use of the death penalty at the federal level and require re-sentencing of those currently on death row.

points.summary: Lateefah will work to create a fair and humane immigration system that disentangles the criminal system from immigration, expands legal pathways to work authorization and citizenship, defends DACA, and ensures Dreamers have a pathway to citizenship and access to the social safety net.
points.quote: She will work to create a fair and humane immigration system that would disentangle the criminal system from the immigration system

points.summary: The campaign commits to breaking up monopolies, banning junk fees, cracking down on price-gouging, protecting Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid, SNAP, and Veterans' Benefits from cuts, and making childcare and family life more affordable.
points.quote: Take on Corporate Greed and Price-Gouging: Break up monopolies, crack down on price-gouging, stop junk fees, and hold corporations accountable when they raise prices while making record profits.

points.summary: The campaign supports lowering premiums, deductibles, and prescription drug prices, capping out-of-pocket costs, protecting Medicare and Medi-Cal, expanding mental health care, and moving toward universal affordable healthcare so no family goes bankrupt from illness.
points.quote: Lower premiums, deductibles, co-pays, prescription drug prices, and out-of-pocket costs — and move toward universal, affordable healthcare so no family goes bankrupt because they got sick.

points.summary: The campaign pledges to protect Title I and IDEA funding, expand tutoring and after-school programs, lower college and career-training costs, protect Pell grants, expand apprenticeships, and treat broadband as basic infrastructure for every student.
points.quote: Protect Title I and IDEA funding and expand tutoring and after-school.

points.summary: The campaign supports cracking down on dealers, gun trafficking, and organized crime while funding community violence prevention, mental health crisis response, reentry programs, and law enforcement accountability paired with transparency and civil rights protections.
points.quote: Crack down on dealers, gun trafficking, and organized crime—focus on the dealers and networks fueling violence, not working families.

points.summary: The campaign commits to cutting energy costs, accelerating clean energy and grid upgrades, holding polluters accountable with polluter-pays rules, protecting clean air and water, and building localized disaster response for wildfires and extreme heat.

points.summary: The campaign pledges to protect reproductive healthcare nationwide, expand equal protection against discrimination in housing, employment, education, and healthcare, and defend civil liberties regardless of race, gender, religion, sexual orientation, or immigration status.
points.quote: Protect reproductive healthcare nationwide—stop federal bans, defend access to contraception and family planning, and protect the right to privacy in healthcare decisions.

points.summary: The campaign advocates ending open-ended military deployments, requiring Congress to authorize war, prioritizing diplomacy and humanitarian assistance over military force, and subjecting national security spending to the same scrutiny as other budget items.
points.quote: We must end open-ended deployments, stop unauthorized air campaigns, and return service members from conflicts that lack clear goals or a responsible conclusion.

points.summary: Sam Liccardo prioritizes accelerating construction of affordable and market-rate housing through bipartisan legislation, cutting red tape, modernizing reviews, and converting vacant office buildings into housing. He authored five bipartisan housing bills, four of which passed both chambers.
points.quote: Leading/co-leading five bipartisan housing bills to accelerate the construction of affordable and market-rate housing

points.summary: The campaign centers on reducing the cost of living for working families, including lowering bank and financial transaction fees, eliminating cost-inflating tariffs, and reducing health insurance premiums through bipartisan legislation.
points.quote: Introduced the bipartisan PACE Act to reduce bank and financial transaction fees for consumers and modernize payment systems.

points.summary: Liccardo introduced the Fix It Act, a bipartisan ACA premium tax credit extension designed to lower health insurance premiums for 22 million Americans while saving taxpayer dollars, securing cosponsors from both parties to break a legislative stalemate.
points.quote: Introduced the Fix It Act, the only bipartisan ACA premium tax credit extension designed to lower health insurance premiums while saving taxpayer dollars.

points.summary: Through Innovation for Good and the Innovation Agenda, Liccardo advocates a pro-innovation framework to keep America competitive in AI and advanced manufacturing, retain skilled international talent, and prepare workers for AI-driven industries through employer-college partnerships.
points.quote: We launched Innovation for Good (I4G) to build a pragmatic, pro-innovation Democratic majority in Congress.

points.summary: Liccardo established the Wildfire Resilience Partnership and the Partnership for the Coastside's Future to coordinate wildfire prevention, coastal resilience, and infrastructure investment. He also advanced efforts to reduce wildfire-related property insurance costs through fire safety investments.
points.quote: Established the Wildfire Resilience Partnership to accelerate wildfire prevention and infrastructure investment across the district.

points.summary: Liccardo authored the MEME Act to ban elected officials from profiting off cryptocurrency schemes, the POCCA Act to prevent unconstitutional withholding of appropriated funds, and the SUN Act to address unlawful military deployments in American cities.
points.quote: Authored H.R. 1712, the MEME Act, to prevent elected officials from profiting from cryptocurrency schemes and other financial conflicts of interest.

points.summary: Liccardo led opposition to federal Continuum of Care changes that would have pushed extremely low-income families into homelessness and secured federal funding for local affordable housing and homelessness reduction projects throughout the district.
points.quote: Led dozens of Members of Congress in successfully opposing proposed changes to the federal Continuum of Care program that would have pushed thousands of extremely low-income families into homelessness.

points.summary: The campaign states advocacy for voting rights, reproductive freedom, and protection of Social Security, Medi-Cal, and CalFresh funding, while opposing cuts to healthcare and food assistance programs impacting working families and seniors.
points.quote: Advocated for voting rights, reproductive freedom, and protection of Social Security, Medi-Cal, and CalFresh funding.

points.summary: Proposes a single-payer, public, nonprofit natural disaster insurance system for every Californian, replacing the privately run FAIR Plan. points.quote: We need to invest in new housing of all types: affordable and subsidized housing, cooperative and land trust models, and market-rate, affordable-by-design building.

points.summary: Treats homelessness as a public health emergency rather than a criminal issue. points.quote: We need to treat homelessness as a public health emergency.

points.summary: Calls for canceling Berkeley's Flock automated license plate reader contract, arguing it has a clear pattern of abuse and misuse that no municipal privacy policy can remedy. points.summary: Kromer prioritizes basic municipal services above all new initiatives: filling potholes, fixing streetlights, cleaning sidewalks, and returning resident calls. He proposes publishing response times monthly for pothole fills, streetlight repairs, and 311 closures as accountability metrics.
points.quote: Smooth streets, working lights, clean sidewalks, calls returned. That's the job, and it comes first.

points.summary: Kromer commits to plain-language budgets, publishing results alongside every contract showing what was paid and what was delivered, and holding a hard line against mid-cycle priority additions that are funded by cutting already-promised services.
points.quote: Plain-language budgets, published results, and a hard line on what we pay for versus what we get.

points.summary: Kromer advocates faster, more predictable permit processes with published median decision times by permit type. For housing specifically, he supports writing design standards first, then permitting what fits them quickly, so applicants do not face years of design review.
points.quote: Faster permits, real response times, performance you can measure. For housing: fast, predictable permits for what fits the neighborhood.

points.summary: Kromer calls for competent public safety and well-maintained parks in District 1 (Ohlone, Cedar Rose, James Kenney, North Waterfront), with a published maintenance schedule and park condition reports kept current to ensure shared spaces remain safe and usable.
points.quote: Competent public safety and well-kept parks — Ohlone, Cedar Rose, James Kenney, North Waterfront — maintained like we mean it.

points.summary: Kromer emphasizes that most homelessness funding comes from federal, state, and county sources. His role would be coordinating those programs, publishing counts of people helped and housed, and fixing what the data shows is not working.
points.quote: The council's job is to make them work together and to say plainly what they bought

points.summary: Kromer supports protecting West Berkeley's industrial-arts economy by keeping land zoned for making, putting the permit process on the public record with steps, costs, and waits, and tracking whether makers remain year over year.
points.quote: A safe place to work, a permit process makers can trust, and land that stays zoned for making. Help them survive; don't zone them out.

points.summary: Kromer criticizes Berkeley for never putting its surveillance contract out to competitive bid across multiple years and roughly two million dollars in spending with a single vendor, and calls for bidding the contract before deciding.
points.quote: Not in 2021, 2023, 2025, or 2026 — through roughly $2 million in proposed spending with one vendor.

points.summary: On corridor upzoning, Kromer supports design standards (shadow, wind, setbacks, street trees) on San Pablo before applications arrive, but would vote no on added heights on Solano and College where no state floor applies, with tenant and small-business protections in the ordinance text.
points.quote: Standards first on San Pablo; no added heights on Solano and College.

points.summary: The campaign calls for more housing production combined with tenant protections, preservation of existing lower-cost housing, permanently affordable homes, and preventing displacement. New development should contribute to neighborhood infrastructure and quality of life.

points.summary: The campaign treats parks, sidewalks, public restrooms, trees, and gathering spaces as essential civic infrastructure. It calls for maintaining and improving public spaces, expanding amenities, and restoring People's Park as public land and ecological space.

points.summary: Calls for real traffic safety on Claremont Avenue including a proper signal at the school zone, sustained speed enforcement, dedicated cyclist lanes, utility undergrounding, street lighting upgrades, and data-driven traffic analysis ahead of the underground bypass project.

points.summary: Calls for real evacuation plans and resident safety standards for District 8's wildland-urban interface, developed in partnership with the fire department and UC Berkeley, to be implemented before the next fire event rather than after.

points.summary: Supports public safety as a fundamental responsibility, clean neighborhoods, well-maintained parks, streets, and sidewalks, with preventive maintenance over delayed repairs and success measured by everyday resident experience rather than statistics alone.
points.quote: Support public safety, clean neighborhoods, parks, streets, sidewalks, and practical approaches to homelessness that balance compassion with community responsibility.

points.summary: Advocates practical approaches to homelessness that balance compassion with community responsibility, while also considering regional cooperation, mental health, housing, and program effectiveness rather than viewing the issue through a single lens.
points.quote: Many residents understandably think about homelessness in terms of neighborhood safety and quality of life. Those concerns are real and deserve attention.

points.summary: Supports smart growth that balances new housing development with supporting infrastructure, protects neighborhood livability, considers long-term community impacts, and plans for future generations while encouraging economic opportunity.
points.quote: Smart growth balances housing, transportation, economic development, infrastructure, parks, schools, and neighborhood character.

points.summary: Committed to responsible financial stewardship: careful budgeting, transparency in how public funds are used, measurable outcomes from investments, long-term fiscal sustainability, and balancing today's needs with tomorrow's obligations.
points.quote: Respect taxpayer dollars through careful budgeting, transparency, measurable outcomes, and long-term fiscal responsibility.

points.summary: Supports transportation improvements as part of smart growth that works for residents, balancing new development with infrastructure needs while improving quality of life and respecting existing neighborhoods.
points.quote: Support housing, economic development, transportation, and infrastructure in ways that improve quality of life while respecting existing neighborhoods.

points.summary: Promotes transparent and responsive government: clear explanations of decisions, meaningful public participation, accountability, understandable communication, and welcoming different perspectives so residents feel informed and able to participate.
points.quote: Promote understandable government, meaningful public participation, accountability, and clear communication about how decisions are made.

points.summary: Fremont should use multiple levers for affordability: protect households now, increase housing availability, lower production costs, grow household capacity, and measure the affordability gap. Subsidy and deed-restricted housing help but structural affordability requires addressing the widening gap between market costs and purchasing power.
points.quote: Affordability requires multiple levers, not a single program.

points.summary: Housing and mobility must be planned as one connected system. Practical alternatives must serve trips residents actually make, not merely assume a mode shift. Elected officials should establish outcomes, demand transparent cumulative analysis, and measure implementation rather than replacing professional engineering judgment.
points.quote: Housing and mobility should be planned as one connected system.

points.summary: Kimberlin advocates for collaborative, practical homelessness solutions tailored to Fremont rather than a one-size-fits-all approach. She voted against the 2025 camping ordinance, successfully pushed to remove its 'aiding and abetting' clause to protect nonprofits, and created a Community Action Forum on Homelessness to sustain cross-jurisdictional coordination.
points.quote: there is no one-size-fits-all approach to addressing homelessness

points.summary: A top stated priority is supporting small businesses and nonprofits in Fremont by leading local businesses, connecting them with resources, and championing education and support for Tri-City nonprofits through her co-founding of the Tri-City Nonprofit Coalition and leadership of the Fremont Education Foundation.
points.quote: Leading local businesses and connecting them with resources.

points.summary: The campaign identifies public safety as a core area of focus alongside smart growth and social/economic development, emphasizing a collaborative approach with City, County, and community members rather than a single-policy stance.

points.summary: Kimberlin frames her entire campaign around bringing accessibility, transparency, and integrity to Fremont City Council, positioning herself as an accessible and transparent leader who ensures every resident feels heard, valued, and represented.
points.quote: I’m running for City Council in District 3 to bring accessibility, transparency and integrity to the people of Fremont.

points.summary: The campaign states she has promoted affordable housing actions in partnership with small businesses and City staff, and her homelessness work includes studying models like Palo Alto Affordable Housing and Lifeline Housing tiny-home units as potential strategies for Fremont.
points.quote: promoted affordable housing actions, coordinated refugee resettlement efforts, and championed COVID economic recovery

points.summary: Kimberlin pledges to work collaboratively with residents to bring jobs to Fremont and grow the community, citing her role managing a $3+ million budget that brings resources to small businesses and nonprofits as evidence of her economic-development track record.
points.quote: I’ll work collaboratively with you to help bring jobs to our city and grow our community.

points.summary: Build more affordable housing for working families, seniors, and people with disabilities, and expand transit-oriented development near BART and bus lines to reduce displacement and make housing more accessible.
points.quote: Building affordable housing gives working families, seniors, and people with disabilities a real chance to live in Fremont without spending the majority of their paycheck on rent.

points.summary: Expand supportive housing and wraparound services to help unhoused individuals stay housed, building on Fremont's existing progress on homelessness.
points.quote: I intend to build on it by expanding supportive housing and the wraparound services that help people stay housed once they get there.

points.summary: Ban private equity firms from purchasing residential property in Fremont to protect housing stock for individual families and first-time homebuyers rather than corporate investors.
points.quote: I will pursue every available legal avenue to protect Fremont's housing stock for individual families and first-time homebuyers, not for corporations seeking a return.

points.summary: Oppose building AI data centers in Fremont, support solar canopies and panels on city property, require native species for all new city plantings, and develop community gardens on idle city land.
points.quote: I oppose it. Our industrial land should serve our community, creating jobs and opportunities for local residents, not server farms for trillion-dollar AI companies.

points.summary: Prohibit Fremont city staff and police from cooperating with or assisting ICE operations, consistent with California law, so all residents can interact with city government without fear.
points.quote: I support a clear policy prohibiting Fremont city staff and police from cooperating with or assisting Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations, consistent with California law.

points.summary: Ensure first responders have adequate training, equipment, mental health support, and community relationships, including investment in de-escalation training and mental health co-responder programs.
points.quote: I support making sure our first responders have the training, equipment, mental health support, and community relationships they need to do their jobs well

points.summary: Reduce traffic by partnering with navigation apps to steer cut-through traffic off neighborhood streets, improve signal timing, build roundabouts, create a pothole map with funded repair timeline, and add protected bike lanes.
points.quote: I'll partner with Google Maps, Waze, and other navigation apps to steer freeway cut-through traffic away from our neighborhood streets

points.summary: Create a Section 115 Trust to set aside dedicated funds for pension obligations, conduct an independent cybersecurity audit and seismic risk assessment, and protect city investments from market volatility.
points.quote: I support creating a Section 115 Trust to set aside extra funds specifically for pension obligations, protecting residents from the future service cuts

points.summary: The campaign commits to continuing investment in technology and additional patrol officers to maintain the 31% crime reduction achieved in 2025 and keep Hayward neighborhoods safe.
points.quote: I will continue investing in technology and staffing arrangements that place more patrol officers in our neighborhoods so we can keep driving crime down

points.summary: The campaign prioritizes completing and adopting the Business Friendly Hayward Plan to streamline permitting, fill vacant buildings, and attract entrepreneurs to open small and large businesses in Hayward.
points.quote: My priority is to complete and adopt the Business Friendly Hayward Plan, which will streamline permitting, focus on filling vacant buildings

points.summary: The campaign aims to establish Hayward as an Education City by building a seamless education-to-career pathway, including guaranteed admission to CSUEB for every Hayward high school graduate and partnerships across schools and colleges.
points.quote: I promised to build a seamless education-to-career pathway so our students and families can succeed right here at home.

points.summary: The campaign addresses Hayward's projected $32 million structural deficit for FY 2026-27 through hiring key leadership, negotiating labor concessions, applying Measure C funds, and tightening operational cost controls to protect core services.
points.quote: I outlined a clear and responsible plan to put Hayward back on strong financial footing.

points.summary: The campaign commits to producing housing for every income level, preserving existing housing so families can live sustainably, and enacting policies that protect renters so they can live with certainty.

points.summary: The campaign pledges continued investment in road improvements to ensure streets are safe for all modes of travel, including pedestrians, drivers, and bicyclists.
points.quote: I will continue investing in road improvements and making sure our streets are safe for pedestrians, drivers, and bicyclists.

points.summary: The campaign works with community partners to open structured, safe services for individuals experiencing homelessness, including the Hayward Navigation Center and Regis Village operated with Bay Area Community Services.
points.quote: Working with Bay Area Community Services to open Regis Village to offer structured and safe services to individuals experiencing homelessness

points.summary: The campaign emphasizes democratic principles, transparency, community engagement, and data-driven decision-making as core governance values, insisting all neighborhoods and families deserve a voice in policy development.
points.quote: Elected leaders must promote democratic principles and listen to families who rely on them to make sound decisions.

points.summary: Jorgens prioritizes maintaining and upgrading parks with new amenities, playgrounds, restrooms, and Wi-Fi; creating a Parks Commission; building a new Community and Arts Center; and expanding library hours to strengthen community gathering spaces.
points.quote: Our City Parks serve as essential spaces for our community to gather and recreate.

points.summary: Jorgens treats public safety as the city's largest budget priority, supporting police staffing and community programs, extending the Alameda County Fire Department contract, updating emergency plans, maintaining road infrastructure, and building two new fire stations.
points.quote: Public Safety is the largest portion of Newark's budget, so ensuring public safety must be a primary focus for the City Council over the next four years.

points.summary: Jorgens supports continued investment in Project Homekey, collaboration with Alameda County and neighboring cities, and pursuing state and federal grants for housing and supportive services to reduce Newark's homelessness.
points.quote: This led to the construction of 125 units of housing for Newark residents experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

points.summary: Jorgens commits to updating Newark's Climate Action Plan, advancing circular economy principles, expanding clean energy generation through solar installations, and positioning the city to access state and federal climate funding.
points.quote: While no city alone can make globally significant progress in addressing climate change, every city must take steps to do what it can.

points.summary: Jorgens supports growing protected bike lanes, improving sidewalk quality, and bringing restaurants and recreational opportunities closer to homes so residents walk rather than drive to other cities.
points.quote: We can do that by growing our network of protected bike lanes, improving the quality of our sidewalks

points.summary: Jorgens commits to passing sustainable budgets, exploring new revenue sources by attracting businesses to strengthen the tax base, and maintaining financial reserves to fund community investments without depleting reserves.
points.quote: Newark’s future will rely on the City being diligent in passing budgets that are sustainable to meet the City’s needs now and in the future.

points.summary: Jorgens advocates for more advisory committees including a Public Art Commission with a youth seat, a student member on the School District Liaison Committee, and a Parks Commission to broaden public participation in city decisions.
points.quote: I believe that the City of Newark will benefit from having more Advisory Committees.

points.summary: Jorgens advocates for flexible land use and zoning policies so businesses can grow their physical spaces, arguing regulations should be applied creatively rather than rigidly. He also supports the re-launched Newark Chamber of Commerce and local business initiatives like the 'Flavors of Newark' restaurant guide.
points.quote: providing flexibility in our land use policies to allow the physical spaces these companies operate at to grow

points.summary: The campaign's top priority is confronting Newark's projected FY 2029 deficit by cutting waste, protecting essential neighborhood services, and maintaining existing infrastructure before committing to new spending, putting the city on a sustainable financial path.
points.quote: With a projected deficit looming in fiscal year 2029, we need disciplined leadership to cut waste, protect essential services, and put Newark on a sustainable financial path.

points.summary: The campaign pledges to equip emergency responders and ensure neighborhood security, specifically advocating that Newark's mutual-aid contracts prioritize local response times rather than subsidizing neighboring cities' coverage gaps after Union City closed Station 30.
points.quote: Newark taxpayers approved public safety funding to safeguard our community, not to subsidize emergency coverage next door.

points.summary: The campaign prioritizes critical road maintenance, street repairs, and traffic improvements, emphasizing preventative maintenance over costly delays, citing worsening street conditions, recurring sinkholes, and increased traffic from new distribution centers.
points.quote: Prioritizing critical road maintenance, street repairs, and traffic improvements.

points.summary: The campaign supports creative, sensible housing solutions tailored to Newark's character, specifically proposing to repurpose surplus city parcels (old fire station site, Mayhew's Landing lot) into affordable homes for working residents beyond the standard 10% inclusionary quota.
points.quote: Rather than settling for the bare-minimum 10% affordable housing quota on new developments, we should partner with organizations to turn these surplus parcels into real, affordable homes for working residents.

points.summary: The campaign commits to addressing homelessness with dignity and accountability, framing it as a compassionate solution that balances compassion with responsible governance.
points.quote: Compassionate solutions: Addressing homelessness with dignity and accountability.

points.summary: The campaign emphasizes stewardship of Newark's 14,000 public trees and the Urban Forest Master Plan, as well as executing the 134-acre Parks Master Plan to deliver shaded trails, upgraded parks, and inclusive playgrounds.
points.quote: From caring for Newark’s 14,000 public trees to shaping our Urban Forest Master Plan, I know real leadership takes both community vision and fiscal discipline.

points.summary: Mitigate climate change effects on East Bay Regional Parks—tree mortality, sea level rise, and wildfire prevention—through reforestation, native vegetation restoration, and pragmatic fuels management.
points.quote: Mitigating the effects of climate change on our parks – tree mortality, sea level rise, and wildfire prevention – with reforestation, native vegetation restoration, and pragmatic fuels management.

points.summary: Expand equitable access to regional parks for all communities and abilities through better outreach, transportation connections, educational programs, and recreation opportunities so more people feel the parks are theirs.
points.quote: Expanding equitable access for all communities and abilities – better outreach, transportation connections, educational programs, and recreation opportunities, so more people see the parks as theirs.

points.summary: Provide strong, transparent stewardship of taxpayer resources for the park district using a pragmatic mix of bonds, climate-resilience grants, philanthropy, and fair fees that visibly go back into facilities people use.
points.quote: Strong, transparent stewardship of taxpayer resources – a pragmatic mix of bonds, climate-resilience grants, philanthropy, and fair fees that go visibly back into the facilities people use.

points.summary: Maintain the balance between conservation and recreation in the park district, treating them as complementary partners rather than opposing priorities, so protecting nature and connecting people to it reinforce one another.
points.quote: I'll keep that balance – conservation and recreation as partners, not opponents.

points.summary: Refuse campaign contributions from developers, fossil fuel interests, or anyone whose interests conflict with the well-being of parks and visitors, pledging to owe only voters' interests when voting on the Board.
points.quote: I am not accepting contributions from developers, fossil fuel interests, or anyone whose interests run counter to the well-being of our parks and visitors.

points.summary: Maintain the balance between conservation and recreation, viewing them as reinforcing rather than opposing goals. Protecting nature and connecting people to nature through recreation should work together to ensure parks thrive for the next generation.
points.quote: The District works because protecting nature and connecting people to it reinforce one another. I'll keep that balance – conservation and recreation as partners, not opponents.

points.quote: I'll push to enforce permitting timelines with automatic escalation if missed

points.summary: The campaign calls for auditing and capping SFPD overtime spending, expanding the Street Crisis Response Team for non-criminal 911 calls, and implementing coordinated block-level investments in lighting and programming. Also demands proper classification of hate crimes in the Castro and dedicated investigation capacity.
points.quote: I'll start there: require supervisor sign-off on all overtime, cap individual overtime hours, and publish department-level overtime data quarterly.

points.summary: The campaign prioritizes prevention over shelter, proposing expanded rapid re-housing and targeted rental assistance for cost-burdened households. points.summary: The campaign supports funding Muni through November ballot measures to avoid a $307 million fiscal cliff, demands route-level on-time performance data be published alongside headway data, and requires an equity analysis before any route elimination serving transit-dependent populations.

points.summary: The campaign proposes requiring new residential and mixed-use developments on transit corridors to include ground-floor spaces built to childcare licensing specs, opening empty rec center rooms for licensed providers, and cutting ELFA voucher enrollment wait from twelve months to ninety days.

points.quote: I'll push for a pre-positioned smoke response plan: air purifier distribution, certified clean-air shelters at rec centers and libraries, and automatic notification when AQI hits hazardous levels.

points.summary: Prioritize very-low-income housing (affordable to preschool teachers, home health aides) over market-rate. points.quote: My plan gets affordable homes permitted faster and cheaper by using the negotiating leverage the city already holds at Parkline and at the USGS campus.

points.summary: Revitalize Downtown Menlo Park by fixing crumbling sidewalks and neglected streetscape, modernizing allowed business types on Santa Cruz Avenue to include community-serving and small-scale commercial recreation, launching Fourth Fridays live music events, and investing in infrastructure to keep the commercial core vibrant.

points.summary: Address Menlo Park's structural budget deficit through fiscal responsibility, logical decision-making, accurate data, and effective execution. As Finance and Audit Commission Chair, she emphasizes analytical rigor and management metrics for creating government efficiencies.

points.summary: Commit to listening to residents and valuing their quality of life, contrasting with her view that the current City Council dismisses neighborhood concerns. She wants decisions that make sense to the people who have to live with them.

points.summary: The city should use its leverage during project review to deepen income restrictions in already-approved developments (e.g., Parkline's 154 units at 60% AMI) to very-low-income levels, costing roughly $90,000 per unit, rather than relying solely on new construction from scratch.
points.quote: It can buy affordability into a building someone else is already constructing, so long as the deal closes before permits issue.

points.summary: The campaign's first stated priority is ensuring strong instruction in reading, math, and science, explicitly conditioned on providing sufficient teacher support so that academic programs can actually function in classrooms.
points.quote: Strong reading, math, and science. With enough teacher support to make it work.

points.summary: The campaign's second priority is that students must first develop independent critical-thinking skills before being introduced to AI tools. The position rejects both hype and panic, emphasizing that technology should help children think harder rather than replace thinking.
points.quote: Kids learn to think for themselves first. Then they learn to use tools like AI. No hype, no panic.

points.summary: The campaign's third priority is that schools must provide mental health support, physical movement, and genuine well-being resources, arguing that students cannot learn effectively without these foundational supports in place.
points.quote: Mental health, movement, and real support. Kids can't learn well without them.

points.summary: The campaign's fourth priority calls for school board governance grounded in real evidence, transparent trade-offs, and follow-through on decisions. The candidate frames herself as an evidence-based question-asker who will explain complex budget and policy decisions in plain language.
points.quote: Real evidence. Clear trade-offs. Decisions the board follows through on.

points.summary: The campaign emphasizes transparency in school funding decisions, particularly around parcel taxes. It commits to providing voters with plain-English data on costs, what has changed, how money would be used, and how effectiveness will be measured, while supporting strong schools.
points.quote: Supporting strong schools and asking hard questions are not opposites. In fact, I believe they belong together.

points.summary: The campaign states that any technology or AI adoption in schools must keep student data privacy and teacher professional judgment as the top safeguards, and that improvement cannot come at the expense of protections that protect people.
points.quote: in schools, that means student privacy and teacher judgment come first

points.summary: The campaign prioritizes strong foundations in reading, math, and science, emphasizing not just adopting good curriculum but ensuring it is implemented well with adequate teacher support to make the curriculum work in practice.
points.quote: Reading, math, science, strong curriculum implementation, and the teacher support that makes good curriculum actually work.

points.summary: The candidate advocates teaching children critical thinking and reasoning skills before introducing AI tools in the classroom, framing it as a measured, non-hyped approach to technology in education rather than panic or uncritical adoption.
points.quote: Teach children how to reason before asking technology to reason for them.
